question.text:
Let $H(x)$ : " $x$ is a happy person", where the universe is the set of all people. Which of the following correctly expresses "There exists at least one happy person"?

  1. $\forall x H(x)$
  2. $\exists x \forall y(H(x) \wedge H(y))$
  3. $\exists x H(x)$
  4. $\neg \forall x \neg H(x)$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Consider the following two logical equivalences that express 'logical laws':
- $ eg \exists x \in D f \equiv orall x \in D eg f$
- $ eg(f ightarrow g) \equiv eg g ightarrow eg f$

Which of these hold?

  1. both
  2. only the first
  3. only the second
  4. none
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Consider the model (men, women, parent_of), and an interpretation in this model:
$M$ domain of men
$W$ domain of women
$P(x, y) \quad y$ is a parent of $x$

You may assume that both parents of all people in $(M \cup W)$ are also in $(M \cup W)$.
Which of the following formulas is not true in this model?

  1. $\forall x \in(M \cup W) \exists y_1 \in M \exists y_2 \in W\left[P\left(y_1, x\right) \wedge P\left(y_2, x\right)\right]$
  2. $\forall x \in W \exists x^{\prime}, x^{\prime \prime} \in W\left[P\left(x, x^{\prime}\right) \wedge P\left(x, x^{\prime \prime}\right)\right]$
  3. $\forall x \in W \exists x^{\prime}, x^{\prime \prime} \in W\left[P\left(x, x^{\prime}\right) \wedge P\left(x^{\prime}, x^{\prime \prime}\right)\right]$
  4. $\forall x \in(M \cup W) \exists y \in(M \cup W)[P(x, y) \vee P(y, x)]$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Let $H(x)$ : " $x$ is a happy person", where the universe is the set of all people. Which of the following correctly expresses "There exists exactly one happy person"?

  1. $\exists x(H(x) \wedge \forall y(H(y) \rightarrow x=y))$
  2. $\exists x \exists y(H(x) \wedge H(y) \wedge x \neq y)$
  3. $\forall x \forall y(H(x) \wedge H(y) \rightarrow x=y)$
  4. $ \exists x H(x) \wedge \exists y H(y) \wedge x \neq y$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Consider the model (men, women, parent_of), and an interpretation in this model:

$M$ domain of men
$W$ domain of women
$P(x, y) \quad y$ is a parent of $x$

You may assume that both parents of all people in ( $M \cup W$ ) are also in $(M \cup W)$.
Which of the following formulas is not true in this model?

  1. $\forall x \in(M \cup W) \exists y_1 \in M \exists y_2 \in W\left[P\left(x, y_1\right) \wedge P\left(x, y_2\right)\right]$
  2. $\forall x \in M \exists x^{\prime}, x^{\prime \prime} \in M\left[P\left(x, x^{\prime}\right) \wedge P\left(x^{\prime \prime}, x\right)\right]$
  3. $\forall x \in M \exists x^{\prime}, x^{\prime \prime} \in M\left[P\left(x, x^{\prime}\right) \wedge P\left(x^{\prime \prime}, x^{\prime}\right)\right]$
  4. $\forall x \in(M \cup W) \exists y \in(M \cup W)[P(x, y) \leftrightarrow P(y, x)]$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic
